own_solution.law: Translational equipartition gives (1/2)m<v²> = (3/2)k_B T, so v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M). With M = 0.032 kg/mol and T = 400 K, v_rms = sqrt(311775) m/s.
assumptions: Classical ideal-gas thermal motion, with speeds measured in the gas rest frame.
For sentences that heat the sample, its temperature at measurement is 500 K.

notes: The amount n cancels between total translational kinetic energy (3/2)nRT and total mass nM. Both amount sentences specify 2 mol. All four heating sentences specify the same temperature increase, 100 K; heating the sample changes its temperature to 500 K, whereas the unrelated block and separate oven have no specified coupling to it. Holding the heated sample in a closed rigid container adds no dependency to the rms-speed formula. The remote heating statements make the presentation slightly artificial.
